title: How does a vendor model earn and retain approval?
body: Define intended use Decision owner and risk tier Test performance Known cases and segments Test dependencies Freshness, coverage and fallback Independent challenge Are limits and evidence adequate? Approve within limits Version and monitoring triggers Monitor live results Overrides, drift and outages Restrict or suspend Fallback, correction and retest Independent validation tests the use case and its dependencies. The accountable owner records operating limits and the evidence required to resume use after a failure.

title: AI governance & RegTech · Step table
body: Step Action Who acts Evidence or outcome 1 Understand the business Action Identify the vendor service, data feed, users and decision it supports. Establish what staff will do during an outage. Who acts Product and vendor owner Evidence or outcome A dependency map and an approved manual fallback. 2 Identify the risks Action Compare expected updates with actual delivery. Identify which customers were screened using stale inputs. Who acts Model risk and compliance Evidence or outcome A dated exposure window and affected segments. 3 Design the controls Action Set conditions for deployment, suspension and rescreening. Require independent challenge of assumptions before approval. Who acts Model owner and independent validator Evidence or outcome Use limits, acceptance criteria and a recorded challenge. 4 Leverage technology Action Test feed freshness and results by segment. Replay known cases on the specified version and investigate differences. Who acts Validation and data teams Evidence or outcome Versioned test results, missed cases and replay totals. 5 Maintain human accountability Action Decide whether to restrict, suspend or restore the service. Authorize restart only after reviewing the affected cases and recovery evidence. Who acts Designated approval authority Evidence or outcome A decision log with conditions, owner and next review. Partner handoff Ask the vendor for the affected versions and a change log. An independent advisor may challenge the validation design. The institution’s approval authority decides whether the service can resume.

title: AI governance & RegTech
body: Before relying on a black-box score, how can an institution show that it works for its customers, channels and intended use? A vendor assurance report can support specified security controls. Test detection separately using known positive and negative examples, feed freshness, subgroup performance and version changes. Provide independent challenge. Decision trade-off A model closer to a block, refusal or filing decision has greater consequences. Tier approvals and fallbacks differently for summarization, prioritization and consequential uses.

title: Match validation to the use case
body: Separate policy summaries, case drafting, risk scoring and decisions that affect customers. Validation should examine inputs, foreseeable failures, human override and the consequences for a customer when the output is wrong.

title: Testing a proprietary model
body: Even when source code is proprietary, an institution can test known cases and counterexamples, obtain version and provenance records, and agree on change notices and suspension triggers. Restrict the tool’s use if material discrepancies remain unexplained.

title: Options for overseeing RegTech
body: Vendor questionnaires, independent assurance and closer oversight of critical services offer different costs and safeguards. Compare substitutability, concentration across institutions and the effect of an outage on reporting. These are options for policy design.

title: Who needs an AI disclosure?
body: Identify the party supplying the generation tool, the party publishing its output and the audience. Establish the content type, use and jurisdiction before deciding whether machine-readable marking, an audience disclosure or another control fits the obligation.

title: AI governance & RegTech · Control matrix
body: Test the decision a tool supports, the inputs it needs and the consequences of a wrong answer. A functioning interface can conceal stale data or a change in model behaviour. Trigger Control Evidence A screening service reports healthy status after an expected update is missed. Compare actual delivery to the source update schedule. Activate an approved fallback and rescreen the affected period. Feed timestamps, fallback log, affected population and rescreen results. A supplier releases a material model update. Compare both versions on known cases and cases from poorly covered segments. Review new errors before approving reliance. Version comparison, test set, segment results and approval record. A critical service becomes unavailable. Exercise the fallback with realistic volumes and assign priority reviews within available capacity. Timed recovery test, queue age, manual capacity and unresolved exceptions. How to measure effectiveness Time from a missed or faulty input to detection and verified restoration. Report the affected population alongside that interval.

title: AI governance & RegTech · Illustrative scenario
body: Illustrative scenario A screening feed stops updating while the system shows healthy status. Compare expected and actual delivery, scope the affected window, activate an approved fallback, rescreen and preserve exceptions and independent validation.

title: AI governance & RegTech · Stakeholder matrix
body: Role Question Evidence Decision or action Regulators How does the institution know an update preserves control over the original risk? Version comparisons, sample results, change approval and scope of reliance. Examine whether the use stays within demonstrated capability. Boards & executives Do multiple critical controls depend on one source or provider? Dependency map, material incidents, fallback tests and exit costs. Set a concentration tolerance and fund contingencies and deadlines. Business & operations Which services can continue if scoring stops or becomes unreliable? Workflow dependencies, operating hours, manual capacity and rehearsed fallback. Restrict a use, switch processing or suspend reliance. AML investigators Can I explain a historical score, verify its inputs and preserve contrary evidence? Timestamps, model version, source evidence, confidence and review trail. Decide the case on independent evidence and refer recurring errors to the model owner. Customers & victims How can I correct records or seek review after a mistaken match? Permitted service explanation, clarifying identification and review channel. Request correction or human review and have the institution track resolution. External partners Can the supplier reproduce a past output and explain data or model changes? Historical versions, feed updates, coverage limits, incident notices and data export capability. Disclose limits and repairs so the institution can decide permitted reliance.

title: Can the institution reproduce the control and verify the repair?
body: Define the obligation Owner, period and population Expected operation Procedure and rule in force Observed operation Transactions, actions and exceptions Reperform the sample Compare expected and actual Retain the evidence Record scope and limitations Scope the failure Root cause and interim control Repair and retest Backfill plus a later sample Decide closure Independent review and sign-off The reviewer needs a defined population and the control version that applied on the day. The remediation owner supplies the fix, and a separate reviewer tests the closure evidence.

title: FINTRAC examinations · Step table
body: Step Action Who acts Evidence or outcome 1 Understand the business Action Walk through one payment rail with the staff who operate it. Establish which transactions should reach monitoring and which procedure applied. Who acts Operations and compliance Evidence or outcome A population definition, source records and the policy version in force. 2 Identify the risks Action Compare source transactions with those received. Identify the missing period, affected customers and the limits of the evidence. Who acts Control owner Evidence or outcome A quantified gap with counts, amounts and unresolved differences. 3 Design the controls Action Cover the gap while the feed is repaired. Assign responsibility for backfill, review of missed items and responses to examination requests. Who acts Remediation lead Evidence or outcome An interim control, a corrective action plan and an evidence request log. 4 Leverage technology Action Replay the affected population. Reconcile counts and values, then sample ordinary cases and exceptions from a later run. Who acts Data team and control tester Evidence or outcome Replay results, sample selections and dated supporting records. 5 Maintain human accountability Action Provide factual corrections with contemporaneous records. Have a separate reviewer test the repair before the issue is closed. Who acts Compliance lead and independent reviewer Evidence or outcome The factual response, unresolved questions and a documented closure test. Partner handoff An advisor can test whether the evidence supports management’s response. The designated compliance contact submits dated facts to the examiner, tracks outstanding requests and assigns each remediation item to an internal owner.

title: FINTRAC examinations
body: If an examiner samples an exception, can the institution reconstruct what happened and test the subsequent fix? A control needs evidence of suitable design, operation during the sample period and effectiveness against its risk. Pair staff walkthroughs with system records to expose gaps in the documented flow. Decision trade-off A demonstration explains design. Samples across periods, channels and exceptions show daily operation. Define the population before judging what the sample leaves uncovered.

title: A requested transaction falls through
body: When a customer withdraws a request or an institution declines it, record the steps already taken, amount and reason it stopped. Preserve facts that support and weaken suspicion, along with when enough information existed to assess the reporting threshold.

title: Reconstructing the control in effect
body: Retrieve the policy and rule versions in force when the case arose. Trace the operator, exceptions, reviews and outcome. If practice and policy diverged, describe the discrepancy, period affected and population exposed.

title: Responding to a finding or notice
body: For each finding, identify agreed points, specific disputed facts, evidence and completed remediation. On receipt of a formal notice, check the response route, deadline and representation requirements against the notice and applicable law. Track formal proceedings and remediation separately.

title: Filing deadlines and retention periods
body: For multiple cash or virtual-currency receipts, reconstruct receipt times and the relationships relevant to aggregation. Determine record retention separately using the sector, record type and event that starts the retention period.

title: FINTRAC examinations · Control matrix
body: Test whether staff can reconstruct a sampled decision using the procedure, data and rule version available on that day. Include exceptions and a later period after any repair. Trigger Control Evidence A new payment channel enters transaction monitoring. Reconcile source and received populations by count and value, then investigate missing and duplicated records. Source totals, ingestion totals, matched IDs and unexplained differences. A sampled case followed a manual override. Ask the operator to replay the decision and verify who approved the override and when it expired. Rule in force, timestamps, exception record and approval trail. A control owner asks to close a remediation item. Independently retest the failed scenario and a later operating period against agreed acceptance criteria. Original finding, test population, retest workpapers and closure decision. How to measure effectiveness Share of sampled decisions a reviewer can reconstruct from contemporaneous evidence, reported separately for routine cases and exceptions.

title: FINTRAC examinations · Illustrative scenario
body: Illustrative scenario A new payment rail only partly reaches monitoring. Reconcile source and received counts and amounts, establish the affected period, backfill and replay, then independently sample both the replay and subsequent normal runs.

title: FINTRAC examinations · Stakeholder matrix
body: Role Question Evidence Decision or action Regulators Were exceptions in the same period detected and addressed? Sampling population, design, operating records and exception handling. Examine evidence of an isolated error or systemic weakness and its reach. Boards & executives What exposure remains and when can remediation be verified? Exposure window, milestones, interim controls and independent retest report. Fund action, set review dates and require residual-risk reporting if delayed. Business & operations What do operators actually do when an exception falls outside the procedure? Shift logs, exception tickets, sign-offs and handoff timestamps. Update procedures so each exception has a recipient and due date. AML investigators Can the decision be reviewed using only information available at the time? Original alert, rule in force, case versions, timestamps and review notes. Reconstruct the original decision and record subsequent facts and reopening criteria separately. External partners Can the provider reproduce inputs and outputs for the incident period? Archives, delivery manifests, versions, incident notices and recovery tests. Support backfill and scope assessment, leaving validation of the fix to the institution.

title: How do fraud response and AML review work in parallel?
body: Receive a credible lead Verify source, time and authority Fraud response Contact customer through trusted channel AML review Assess activity and counterparties Protect or seek recall Record authority and payment status Decide reporting Preserve evidence and rationale Reconcile outcomes Prevented, recovered and returned Follow up Victim support and control feedback Customer protection and compliance reporting can proceed at the same time. Each team records its authority and decisions, then reconciles its outcome with the other team.

title: Fraud disruption & law enforcement · Step table
body: Step Action Who acts Evidence or outcome 1 Understand the business Action Trace a reported scam payment from the customer’s instruction to the last point where intervention is possible. Who acts Fraud operations Evidence or outcome Payment status, relevant parties and the remaining intervention window. 2 Identify the risks Action Verify the signal and the customer’s immediate exposure. Check timing and identity, including whether the account holder may be a victim. Who acts Fraud investigator Evidence or outcome Signal source, verification time and grounds for the proposed action. 3 Design the controls Action Assign customer contact and any authorized hold or recall. Open a parallel AML review with its own decision owner. Who acts Fraud lead and AML lead Evidence or outcome Two linked work records with authority, owners and deadlines. 4 Leverage technology Action Match transaction references, partner responses and timestamps. Track funds held, recovered and returned as distinct events. Who acts Payments and fraud analysts Evidence or outcome An outcome ledger that prevents double counting the same funds. 5 Maintain human accountability Action Decide the customer’s next action and document the AML disposition independently. Use a designated law-enforcement liaison when a referral is warranted. Who acts Authorized fraud and AML decision-makers Evidence or outcome Customer follow-up, reporting rationale and the record of any authorized referral. Partner handoff A designated liaison can coordinate an actionable lead with a financial crime task force or law-enforcement partner under the applicable authority. Fraud operations follows up with the customer while the AML team assesses reporting.

title: Fraud disruption & law enforcement
body: Between the first scam signal and irreversible payment, who can intervene lawfully and who owns subsequent intelligence and evidence? Fraud teams address immediate harm while AML staff independently assess suspicious flows. Prevention, holds, recovery, return and criminal outcomes are distinct measures with different denominators and time windows. Decision trade-off Timely cross-sector signals can protect customers. Operational intelligence may still lack evidential provenance or process, so establish purpose, authority and minimum necessary disclosure.

title: Parallel fraud and AML decisions
body: While a payment may still be interruptible, identify who is authorized to contact the victim, platform or receiving institution. Preserve the timeline in parallel so AML staff can assess reporting and disclosure obligations independently.

title: From a shared lead to usable intelligence
body: When an outside party shares a phone number, account or wallet lead, record its source, timing and restrictions. Look for matching internal activity and state confidence in the identity link. Information exchange depends on an authorized route and its disclosure conditions.

title: Making sense of disruption outcomes
body: Count victim contacts, blocked transfers, frozen funds, recoveries and returns separately. One case may involve several interventions. A success rate requires a defined denominator and records that distinguish interventions from unique cases.

title: Protecting a victim after a deceptive authorization
body: A customer may personally authorize a transaction or wallet permission while misunderstanding its scope. Ask whom the customer intended to pay and why, reconcile the timing and subsequent movement, and choose an intervention suited to the customer’s exposure.

title: Fraud disruption & law enforcement · Control matrix
body: Connect an urgent fraud signal to the team that can still act on the payment. Track customer protection, reporting decisions and final financial outcomes separately. Trigger Control Evidence A customer reports a scam while a payment is still pending. Verify the report through a trusted channel and route the payment to a person authorized to intervene. Signal time, payment state, callback result and authorized action. A partner supplies a lead about another transaction. Check source, purpose, permitted recipients and the minimum details needed before passing the lead on. Provenance, disclosure basis, transmitted fields and receipt confirmation. One incident appears in both a hold report and a recovery report. Trace the funds through hold, release, recovery and return. Record each status change against the same incident. Payment reference, status history, amounts and evidence of return. How to measure effectiveness Median time from verified signal to authorized action for payments still within an intervention window. Report customer returns separately from amounts temporarily held.

title: Fraud disruption & law enforcement · Conference example, paraphrased
body: Conference example, paraphrased Linking a telecom impersonation signal with bank transfer information created an opportunity for intervention. Trace signal time, verification, authorized action and client outcome. The oral figures remain unverified.

title: Fraud disruption & law enforcement · Stakeholder matrix
body: Role Question Evidence Decision or action Regulators Are the purpose, authority and limits of sharing and intervention documented? Legal basis, access log, minimum disclosure and reporting decision. Review permitted sharing and suspicious-transaction handling separately. Boards & executives What harm was observably reduced, and how confidently can outcomes be attributed? Outcome definitions, amount categories, observation windows, false stops and complaints. Evaluate investment using intervention time and client outcomes, documenting uncertainty. Business & operations Can the payment still be paused or recalled, and who authorizes it? Payment status, rail deadlines, authority policy and receiving-party acknowledgement. Take authorized action within the intervention window and set a review time. AML investigators How can a victim be protected while preserving facts for later investigation? Transaction chronology, independent callback result, original signal and action rationale. Document protection, STR assessment and external referral as separate decisions. Customers & victims How can I verify the caller safely and track my funds? Trusted channel, payment reference, provider responses and incident reference. Verify and follow up using a known trusted channel and retain communications. External partners What can a telecom provider, recipient institution and police each verify? Signal confidence, permitted fields, retained records and lawful requests. Share the minimum permitted information and distinguish operational leads from formal evidence gathering.

title: Which decision addresses the cause of a control gap?
body: Exposure signal Backlog, missed coverage or harm Establish the cause Population, duration and uncertainty Capacity constraint Staffing and priority coverage Incomplete intake Reconcile and repair the feed Unproductive rules Tune and independently validate Decide resources and risk Options, rationale and risk owner Verify the outcome Interim control, retest and review date Management compares options against exposure and time. The board or delegated authority records its decision and the conditions that would require another review.

title: Boards & risk governance · Step table
body: Step Action Who acts Evidence or outcome 1 Understand the business Action Describe the product change and which customers, channels and teams it affected. Establish how the queue grew. Who acts Business sponsor Evidence or outcome A baseline showing volume, backlog age and high-risk cases. 2 Identify the risks Action Separate a shortage of investigators from missing monitoring data or low-value alerts. Estimate the exposure from each. Who acts Risk owner and monitoring lead Evidence or outcome A cause analysis with denominators, uncertainty and residual exposure. 3 Design the controls Action Compare temporary staffing, an interim review and a feed repair. Set a limit and review date for each temporary measure. Who acts Management and control owners Evidence or outcome Options paper with cost, time to reduce exposure and fallback. 4 Leverage technology Action Use reconciled feed counts and queue-age trends to test which option is working. Show high-risk items separately. Who acts Management information team Evidence or outcome A dashboard with dated sources, coverage gaps and overdue items. 5 Maintain human accountability Action Record management’s recommendation, the authorized decision and any challenge. Return to the board or delegate with independent retest results. Who acts Board or delegated authority Evidence or outcome Decision minutes, named action owner, residual risk and follow-up date. Partner handoff A third-party advisor can challenge assumptions in a board paper. Compliance identifies any applicable regulatory engagement. The board or its delegate records the decision, residual exposure and review date.

title: Boards & risk governance
body: How should a board choose between more investigators, a data repair and a change to monitoring rules? The same backlog can arise from capacity limits, unproductive alerts or missing data. Establish the cause, then compare cost, exposure window, ownership and acceptance evidence on one page. Decision trade-off More staff can shorten a queue while transactions missing from intake stay unseen. Name separate owners for interim coverage and the longer-term data fix.

title: What decision does the board need to make?
body: Put the exposure, affected business, risk tolerance and requested decision on the first page. For each option, show cost, delivery time and remaining risk. After the decision, record the owner and next review date.

title: Comparing prevention and remediation costs
body: Estimate preventive investment from the volume of high-risk cases requiring review and available capacity. Remediation can involve lookbacks, outside support and service restrictions. Show the scope and assumptions that produce the range.

title: Governing private-to-private sharing
body: Before a private exchange, establish the mechanism, eligibility, purpose and information permitted. Retain the basis, recipient and approval for the disclosure and track use restrictions. Regulatory reporting and disclosures to law enforcement each have their own authority.

title: Translating regulatory change into action
body: For each change, record the jurisdiction, official text, commencement status, affected entity and owner. Use different case exercises for directors and front-line teams to test whether they can identify when the new requirements call for escalation.

title: Boards & risk governance · Control matrix
body: Give decision-makers the cause, exposure and options behind a risk indicator. A temporary workaround needs a capacity estimate, an expiry date and a clear return to normal control. Trigger Control Evidence A high-risk backlog grows after a product launch. Separate increased volume, poor alert quality and missing data before comparing staffing, tuning and repair options. Queue age by tier, QA samples, source reconciliation and an options paper. A critical failure prompts an emergency override. Name the approving authority, cap the scope and duration, and schedule a retrospective review of affected decisions. Timestamped approval, affected decisions, compensating checks and expiry. A remediation milestone slips. Reassess residual exposure and the sustainability of interim controls. Record the decision and next review date. Issue age, revised capacity estimate, decision rationale and accountable owner. How to measure effectiveness Share of open high-risk issues past their approved review date. Show the age and residual exposure of each overdue issue.

title: Boards & risk governance · Illustrative scenario
body: Illustrative scenario Overdue high-risk cases coincide with a partial new-channel feed. Management presents the denominator and impact for each, then proposes interim manual review, a feed repair and a time-bound independent retest.

title: Boards & risk governance · Stakeholder matrix
body: Role Question Evidence Decision or action Regulators When did the board learn of the issue and how did it track remediation? Escalation chronology, minutes, issue register and retest evidence. Assess whether oversight and challenge translated into follow-through. Boards & executives What risk remains under each option and what does a quarter of delay imply? Metrics with baselines and denominators, material assumptions, options and review dates. Approve resources within mandate or request revisions, recording the basis. Business & operations Which team and shift inherit the workload from an interim control? Transaction windows, exception volumes, capacity and client waiting times. Commit to sustainable coverage, handoffs and exit criteria for temporary measures. AML investigators Which priority cases are constrained by data or capacity? Age by risk tier, QA defects and anonymized case illustrations. Recommend an evidence-led priority and identify remaining information needs. Customers & victims How will legitimate transactions be affected during remediation? Affected service, processing time, complaints and corrections. Raise a service query or complaint so the operator can address individual harm.

title: Which explanation fits the player’s activity?
body: Build the player timeline Funding, play, incentives and cash-out Test competing explanations Check observations and permissions Ordinary play Compare profile and play history Financial crime Test source, links and incentive abuse Player harm Assess welfare indicators Document disposition Record contrary evidence Refer to AML or fraud Assess reporting independently Offer player support Use authorized welfare channels AML, fraud and responsible-gaming teams have different mandates. Document the evidence for each referral and the records that were unavailable to the decision-maker.

title: Gaming & casino financial crime · Step table
body: Step Action Who acts Evidence or outcome 1 Understand the business Action Join one player’s deposits, actual play, incentives and cash-out. Identify which operator or service provider holds each record. Who acts Gaming operations Evidence or outcome A player timeline with payment references, play records and staff observations. 2 Identify the risks Action Compare ordinary play, bonus abuse, laundering and signs of gambling harm. Test explanations for limited play or adjacent-machine use. Who acts AML, fraud and player-protection reviewers Evidence or outcome Evidence for each hypothesis and gaps requiring follow-up. 3 Design the controls Action Define separate escalation routes for fraud, AML and player support. Allow concurrent referrals when needs overlap. Who acts Operator and relevant control owners Evidence or outcome Documented referral criteria, permissions and response owners. 4 Leverage technology Action Match payment and gameplay identifiers and timestamps. Check for shared instruments, duplicate events and missing activity. Who acts Gaming analytics team Evidence or outcome A reconciled timeline with source and confidence for each link. 5 Maintain human accountability Action Record each authorized decision independently and confirm handoffs. Check whether any player-support action reached the customer. Who acts Designated AML, fraud and player-protection leads Evidence or outcome A reasoned disposition for each concern and evidence of follow-up. Partner handoff The operator requests missing play or payment records through the agreed channel. Designated staff route supported concerns to the appropriate AML, fraud or player-protection function and document any authorized external referral.

title: Gaming & casino financial crime
body: Where an operator holds player data and another entity has reporting responsibilities, who can explain unusual behaviour? Read deposits alongside play, timing, withdrawals, promotions, known affordability and funding source. Gambling harm, incentive abuse, ordinary play and laundering can produce overlapping signals with different evidence and referral needs. Decision trade-off Cross-province analysis may reveal hidden patterns, yet common branding does not establish a shared data entitlement or responsibility. Map entities, data permissions and operating arrangements, flagging blind spots.

title: Licensing, accountability and access
body: Map who manages the gaming activity, operates the platform, processes payments and holds player data. Identify the records needed for due diligence, monitoring and escalation, then test that the accountable party can obtain them in time.

title: Ongoing review of gaming merchants
body: Check where the merchant may offer each product and connect the registered entity with websites, payment routes and settlement counterparties. Review new domains or collection routes against the authorization and documented business purpose.

title: Assessing player harm and suspicious funds
body: Increasing deposits, frequent withdrawals or financial strain can have several explanations. Use player history, play relative to funding, source of funds and customer contact to decide separately whether responsible-gambling support and an AML investigation are warranted.

title: Loyalty incentives and false positives
body: Promotions can temporarily change ordinary player behaviour. Test alerts against product rules, offer periods and comparable player activity before interpreting multi-account links, repeated funding sources or connected withdrawals.

title: Gaming & casino financial crime · Control matrix
body: Assess deposits and withdrawals alongside actual play, promotional terms and the player's circumstances. The same signal can call for a responsible-gaming referral, a fraud review or an AML assessment. Trigger Control Evidence Large deposits are followed by limited play and a rapid withdrawal. Reconstruct the betting and payment timeline and test ordinary explanations and the source of funds. Player and payment records, wagers, cash-out details and competing explanations. Payment behaviour changes during a promotion. Check eligibility, actual play and linked payment instruments. Assess promotion misuse and financial-crime indicators separately. Offer terms, play history, verified links and reason for each referral. Repeated losses or customer contact indicate possible gambling harm. Route the concern to trained responsible-gaming staff and assess any separate financial-crime indicators within authorized roles. Observed behaviour, referral time, follow-up and access-controlled case record. How to measure effectiveness Share of sampled cases where the reviewer could distinguish the reason for each AML, fraud or responsible-gaming disposition and verify the handoff.

title: Gaming & casino financial crime · Conference example, paraphrased
body: Conference example, paraphrased A player used two adjacent slot machines. Compare payment, actual play, cash-out and staff observations, test ordinary-play explanations, then decide AML escalation and player support separately.

title: Gaming & casino financial crime · Stakeholder matrix
body: Role Question Evidence Decision or action Regulators Can the supervised entity obtain the payment and betting records its controls require? Local authorization, operating agreement, data handoff inventory, exceptions and report samples. Examine statutory responsibility, operational control and data gaps. Boards & executives What risks become unobservable if an operator or platform withholds data? Data dependencies, uncovered channels, compensating controls, complaints and remediation. Require data access, restrict exposure or revisit contracts and review arrangements. Business & operations Can each player transaction be joined to betting and promotions? Player identifiers, payment and wagering logs, promotion terms and rail reconciliation. Repair missing joins and exception handoffs, assigning owners in procedures. AML investigators Could play, promotions or harm explain the anomaly, and what contradicts each account? Wagering and cash-out patterns, source of funds, behaviour, staff observations and counterevidence. Document the grounds for AML, fraud and responsible-gambling referrals separately. Customers & victims Where can a player seek help for financial harm or an account restriction? Player account, service record, available support and complaint arrangements. Seek support or correction through the right channel and obtain follow-up. External partners What evidence can platform and payment partners lawfully provide for reconciliation? Data definitions, entitlements, references, delivery times and missing-record lists. Confirm delivery scope and unresolved gaps, with an auditable exception handoff.

title: How does an AI-assisted case file reach a human decision?
body: Classify case data Sensitivity and permitted environment Reconcile transactions Deterministic amounts and timestamps Qualify attribution Hash, label source, date and confidence Draft from permitted evidence Attach source IDs to material claims Human review Are claims and uncertainties supported? Correct or escalate Resolve gaps and log edits Authorize disposition Record rationale and filing decision The reviewer retains responsibility for the disposition. Corrections return to the evidence-linked draft, with an audit trail of the change and its reason.

title: Crypto AML & AI automation · Step table
body: Step Action Who acts Evidence or outcome 1 Understand the business Action Define the case question, permitted data and tools, and the decisions a person must make. Identify where customer information may be processed. Who acts Investigations and data owners Evidence or outcome An approved data path, case purpose and named reviewer. 2 Identify the risks Action Test an indirect wallet link against timing, source labels and customer activity. Identify where a draft could overstate attribution. Who acts Crypto investigator Evidence or outcome Transaction hashes, dated label sources and competing explanations. 3 Design the controls Action Require source references for material claims and independent review of consequential decisions. Provide a manual route when evidence is incomplete. Who acts AML control owner Evidence or outcome Review criteria, escalation conditions and a manual fallback. 4 Leverage technology Action Use code to reconcile amounts and times. In the approved environment, build the draft from evidence references and preserve qualifiers. Who acts Analyst using approved tools Evidence or outcome Reproducible calculations and a draft tied to dated records. 5 Maintain human accountability Action Correct any claim that turns a possible link into a confirmed one. Have the authorized reviewer record the reporting or closure decision. Who acts Authorized AML reviewer Evidence or outcome Final narrative, material edits, rationale and review time. Partner handoff A blockchain analytics provider can explain a label’s source and confidence. The investigator corroborates it with transaction records. A designated liaison handles any authorized referral, and a human reviewer signs the case decision.

title: Crypto AML & AI automation
body: How can AI speed crypto AML case preparation while every material claim remains traceable to evidence? Separate calculation, data routing and narrative drafting. Use deterministic tools for amounts and times, an approved model for evidence-linked drafts and an authorized reviewer for contrary evidence and reporting decisions. Decision trade-off An external model may reduce drafting time while client data, wallet labels and STR drafts carry confidentiality risks. Internal models still need access, log-retention and inference controls.

title: What may an AI agent execute?
body: Authorize reading, drafting, proposing transactions and moving money separately. If a tool can move funds, specify amount and counterparty limits, independent approvals, a traceable action history and a way to suspend execution.

title: Tracing an AI-drafted STR to evidence
body: Populate times, amounts and parties from verified fields. A reviewer should trace material statements to evidence, flag unresolved inferences and record reasons for edits. The authorized person makes the filing decision.

title: Personal devices and unapproved AI
body: Use a training scenario to trace which services receive case text after it leaves the case system, who can access it and how long it persists. Provide approved tools and a route for questions, then test staff with a comparable sensitive-data scenario.

title: Handing off a 24-hour payment incident
body: On-chain confirmation, bank payout and human review can keep different hours. An overnight handoff should identify the asset’s last known location, remaining interventions, authorized contacts and time last checked. The incoming team verifies the position before taking ownership.

title: Crypto AML & AI automation · Control matrix
body: Combine on-chain evidence, fiat records and human review across a 24/7 market. Preserve uncertainty in address attribution and keep protected data within approved processing routes. Trigger Control Evidence An analytics provider flags indirect wallet exposure. Verify the chain, transaction and label date. Record the provider's confidence and any evidence against the proposed attribution. Transaction hash, label snapshot, path description and review rationale. A high-priority alert arrives outside business hours. Route it to the duty team with the relevant intervention window and require acknowledgement of the handoff. Alert time, duty roster, acknowledgement and time of review. An AI-generated case draft states an uncertain link as confirmed. Verify material claims against source records, correct the attribution and retain human ownership of the disposition. Evidence IDs, dated source snapshots, draft changes and reviewer sign-off. How to measure effectiveness Share of sampled material claims traceable to a dated source and the level of confidence it supports. Review out-of-hours cases as a separate sample.

title: Crypto AML & AI automation · Illustrative scenario
body: Illustrative scenario A provider flags indirect exposure at an external wallet. The analyst checks hashes, label dates and provenance, corrects a draft that changed “possible link” into “confirmed illicit,” and preserves the edit trail.

title: Crypto AML & AI automation · Stakeholder matrix
body: Role Question Evidence Decision or action Regulators Can the final narrative be traced to transactions and judgments available at the time? Source snapshots, transaction evidence IDs, human edits and approval records. Review reporting basis, completeness and timeliness. Boards & executives Is time saved accompanied by more attribution errors or privacy incidents? QA by use case, material error rates, review effort and exception incidents. Set pilot scope, expansion criteria and stop conditions. Business & operations Who takes a night alert or case during a model outage? Duty roster, triage rules, manual-takeover tests and handoff acknowledgement. Reserve human coverage and escalation times for priority work. AML investigators Is each link an observed fact, provider label or inference? Hashes, values, source and timestamps, confidence and alternative explanations. Own the case and filing decisions and assess any restriction under separate authority. Customers & victims Which sensitive details reach a model, and could an error affect service? Permitted-use information, correction channel, service impact and follow-up records. Use the available channel to correct information or request human handling. External partners How does a blockchain provider communicate uncertainty in indirect or cross-chain exposure? Label provenance, observation date, chain coverage, confidence and gaps. Deliver qualified intelligence and notify users of material attribution changes.

title: Assessment manual for compliance examinations
body: FINTRAC The manual follows an examination from scoping to findings. It explains how examiners use interviews, policies and transaction samples to test whether controls operate in practice.

title: Financial transaction reporting thresholds and deadlines
body: FINTRAC FINTRAC lists the triggers and deadlines by report type. For completed or attempted transactions, a suspicious transaction report is due as soon as practicable once there are reasonable grounds to suspect money laundering, terrorist financing or sanctions evasion.

title: Private-to-private information sharing
body: FINTRAC Reporting entities can share personal information under an approved code of practice. The guidance sets out who can participate and what conditions apply to each disclosure.

title: Stablecoin issuer framework
body: Bank of Canada The Bank’s supervision framework for fiat-backed stablecoins focuses on high-quality liquid reserves and redemption at face value. Draft implementing regulations were published in Part I of the Canada Gazette.

title: Retail payments supervisory framework
body: Bank of Canada This guide explains how payment functions, geographic scope and exclusions determine who must register. The test for electronic funds transfers covers Canadian and foreign currencies and excludes digital currencies.

title: Guideline E-23 · Model Risk Management (2027)
body: OSFI The revised guideline takes effect on 1 May 2027 for federally regulated financial institutions within its scope. It ties how models are reviewed, approved and monitored to their inherent risk.

title: AI Act Article 50 · Transparency duties
body: European Commission The Commission explains the duties that apply from 2 August 2026. Providers may have to mark generated content in a machine-readable format, and deployers may have to disclose when they present deepfakes or other covered content.

title: How OSFI and FINTRAC work together
body: OSFI OSFI supervises the financial soundness of federally regulated institutions, and FINTRAC oversees anti-money laundering and anti-terrorist financing compliance. The page explains how the agencies share relevant supervisory information.

title: Steps to Join the Ontario Market
body: iGaming Ontario Online gaming operators entering Ontario must complete steps with two bodies. The guide lists what operators need for AGCO registration and for an operating agreement with iGaming Ontario.

title: Maple Disruption 2.0
body: Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre The November 2026 operation brought together police, financial institutions and other partners to disrupt services used in fraud. The report gives separate figures for disruptive actions, reported losses and money recovered.
